mechanism: Both drugs have anticholinergic properties and CNS depressant effects; tolterodine is metabolized by CYP2D6 and CYP3A4, while methocarbamol may have minor CYP450 interactions.
action: Monitor for increased anticholinergic side effects (dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, dizziness) and CNS depression; counsel on fall risk and adjust doses if adverse effects emerge.
